issue.title: test_nested_agent_check_keeps_parent_and_never_queues sees zero started check children under load

task_type_fields.evidence:
Proposed by phase sase-1vb.4 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #2) of epic sase-1vb; filed by the sase-1vb land agent.

Failed twice in independent hosted runs on 2026-11-26, both on master-era trees:
- CI on PR #319 (core-pin-ratchet branch), run 45787083765 (head fbf0071273)
- CI Telemetry test-cost, run 45787348404 on master 32b0d45935 (gw2, Python 3.13.18)

Failure, at tests/tool/test_admission_processes.py:472:

    assert len(_started_children(w)) == 1
    AssertionError: assert 0 == 1  (where [] = _started_children(_World(...)))

The preceding steps passed. The outer check wrapper run appeared with parent_run_id None. The inner run with parent_run_id == outer run_id appeared. `_record(inner_run) is None` held, so no admission queue record existed. The test then asserts once, with no wait, that exactly one check child has started. Under load the durable inner run row can land before the child process writes its started marker, which would make this a missing semantic wait. That is unconfirmed. The alternative is a real nested-admission defect where the inner check never starts its child, and that would be a product bug in the property this test guards ("never queues").

It did not fail in Full CI 45849428321 or Master Gate 45846683375 / 45861705482 on later tips, so it is intermittent. Phase sase-1vb.4 found no shared root with the four Master Gate flakes it fixed. Owner: none found (searched test_admission_processes / nested_agent_check / never_queues).
